title: My God, Permit My Tongue
description: My God, Permit My Tongue in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 63, part 4, headed “Seeking God”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, per-mit my tongue This joy, to call thee mine, And let my ear-ly cries pre-vail To taste thy love di-vine.

lines: This joy, to call thee mine,
And let my early cries prevail
I long to find my place,
Thy power and glory to behold,
No joy can be compar'd to this,
To serve and please the Lord.
To thee I'll lift my hands,
And praise thee while I live;
Not the rich dainties of a feast
I call my God to mind;
I think how wise thy counsels are,
Since thou hast been my help,
I follow where my Father leads,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
